newsitem.title: USA: MagCorp says price cut due to inventory hike.
newsitem.headline: MagCorp says price cut due to inventory hike.

text.p: Magnesium Corp of America's cut in North American primary magnesium prices from January were just a modest adjustment to reflect a rise in global stocks, Howard Kaplan, the company's vice president of sales and marketing said.
"We just made a small adjustment here to reflect the fact that inventories have increased a little bit, though not to levels that we consider onerous," Kaplan said.
Last month the International Magnesium Association reported that global stocks at the end of the third quarter were up 5,000 tonnes to 38,400 tonnes compared to the end of the second quarter.
Stocks have recovered from a low of about 17,000 tonnes.
The IMA also reported that primary magnesium shipments in the first nine months of the year were down on the same period last year.
Earlier Wednesday MagCorp said its primary magnesium price from January 1, 1997 will be $1.80 per pound for truckload quantities delivered in the U.S., down from $1.93 set in September 1995.
Officials at rival producers Hydro Magnesium and Dow Magnesium were not immediately available to say if they have or will cut their own list prices in North America.

"We see prices staying pretty stable in 1997 and I expect 1997 to be a year of record demand," Kaplan said. "There is little new capacity coming on and the Israelis seem a little late coming on and a lot of their stuff is committed to VW."
Israel's new Dead Sea magnesium works is in the process of starting up.
MagCorp left its magnesium alloy price unchanged at $1.70 per pound.
"We see the alloy market as staying pretty steady and being a long-term growth market," Kaplan said. Alloy is largely used to make auto components.
